page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below them, two medallion engravings side by side, each with its legend printed around the rim. Under them, one column of text in roman type with two entries, the second ending in italic verse. A gathering signature sits at the lower right of the text block. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: LIVIA MEDULLINA, cognomine Camilla, è ge-
nere antiquo Dictatoris M. Furij Camilli (cuius meminimus
in priori huius operis parte pag.125.) eo ipso die qui erat nuptiis
Claudij Imp. atque huius Medullinæ destinatus, morbo periit.
tre nata, eidē Claud. Imp. nupsit, cum qua diuortiū ille fecit, ob
libidinū probra, & homicidij in virum fuspitionē. ex hac Clau-
diam fuscepit, & Drusum, quem puberē amisit, pyro per lusum
in sublime iactato, & haitu [?] oris excepto strangulatum, cui & fi-
liam Seiani desponderat. Vide ut supra. Cæterum de Seiano ho-
mine præpotente ac prædiuite, cui tandem fortuna nouercā se
præstitit, vide Iuvenalem Satyra 10. nam huius exēplo nimias
opes, potentiam ac fastum multis exitio esse ostēdit Iuvenalis,

l.i: / Invidia, mergit longa, atque insignis honorum /
Ipsas deinde rotas bigarum impacta securis /
Jam stridunt ignes, jam follibus atque caminis /
Ardet adoratum populo caput, & crepat ingens /
Seianus, deinde ex facie toto orbe secunda, /
Pone domi lauros, duc in capitolia magnum /

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed in the engraved rims; "PLAUSIA" read with [?] as the second legend is partly cramped. "haitu" is doubtful (possibly a misprint for hausu). The Greek-free page has no catchword. The verse is set as one stanza with the lines separated by " / ". Spelling of u/v and i/j normalised as per the rules; printed spellings such as diuortiū, suspitionē, pag.125. and restémque are left as printed.
